title: A Systematic Review on Arsenic Toxicity in Aquatic Ecosystems: Mechanistic Insights and Impacts on Fish Health
content:
ABSTRACT

Arsenic contamination of aquatic ecosystems is a serious worldwide concern, with natural and anthropogenic sources leading to chronic exposure in surface and ground waters at concentrations often above safe regulatory thresholds. This review critically synthesizes the findings from research published throughout the period 2000–2026 on the environmental behaviors of arsenic and its toxicological impacts on fish species. It also outlines ecological niches, speciation, and mobility controls on arsenic bioavailability, and traces its bioaccumulation and trophic transfer from water and sediment through primary producers and consumers into fish tissue, where inorganic species, especially arsenite, are markedly more toxic than organic, methylated forms. At the cellular level, arsenic-induced reactive oxygen species activate Keap1–Nrf2–ARE-mediated antioxidant defense. Beyond this role, downstream apoptosis and genotoxic DNA damage occur, resulting in organ-specific pathology in the gills, liver, kidney, skin, and reproductive and immune systems, with associated impairment of growth, survival, and reproductive fitness. Furthermore, a comparative evaluation of traditional and innovative arsenic removal technologies based on grounds of removal effectiveness, cost, and operational efficiency was presented. It was concluded that no particular mitigation approach completely eliminates arsenic-related toxicity to fish during prolonged environmental exposure, necessitating a multifaceted management strategy that includes source control, appropriate technology selection based on local resource limitations, and ongoing biomarker-driven ecological monitoring. Future research must standardize bioaccumulation protocols across species, validate the remediation methods, evaluate the arsenic toxicity in the presence of climate stressors, and propose regulatory measures to balance aquaculture and water quality standards with organ level biomonitoring.
